newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian experts favour Yakovlev's Fokker bid.
newsitem.headline: Russian experts favour Yakovlev's Fokker bid.

text.p: Russian government and aviation industry experts said Russian plane-maker Yakovlev should go ahead with a plan to buy bankrupt Dutch plane-maker Fokker NV, a senior Yakovlev official said on Thursday.

Aviatsionnaya Korporatsiya Yakovlev vice-president Arkady Gurtovoi told Reuters the experts, appointed by the government this summer to study the proposed bid, visited Fokker recently and prepared a report with "positive conclusions".
"We are waiting for the goverment's final decision and hope to get it later this month," Gurtovoi said. The report was passed to the cabinet five days ago.

There were two possibilities. Either the government could approve Yakovlev's 370 million guilder bid for NV Koninklijke Nederlandse Vliegtuigenfabriek Fokker, or the cabinet could ask Yakovlev to amend the plan, he said.

Dutch technical engineering group Stork NV bought the profitable maintenance and services arm of the bankrupt company, Fokker Aviation, but has said it would sell it back to a buyer of the plane-making activities if this was necessary for Fokker's survival.
Last week Fokker said South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries was carrying out exclusive due diligence procedures on the Dutch company.
Fokker went bankrupt in March this year, and soon after Yakovlev first expressed interest in buying the company.
